parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish desman (“musk” as in desmanråtta “muskrat”), from older desma, desme, from Middle Low German dēsem, from Old Saxon desamo, alteration of *besamo, from Late Latin bisamum (“musk”), from Hebrew בשם (bāśām, bōśem). Doublet of Bisam and Balsam.

parole.significato: skerry (flat, rocky isle, especially in Scandinavia)
parole.testo: 17th century, backformation from Swedish skären, definite plural of skär n, perhaps through Middle Low German schēr(e) (“reef”). All eventually from Old Norse sker.
